messages.author: 7eed7eee7dd92cf3
messages.subject: Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated.
parts:
Hi camtrapR users, 

I have encountered the following issue when trying to build detection histories for several species at once, as illustrated by the author of the package here:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr5.html#data-preparation

I have contacted him some months ago and he told me to install the latest version from github, however the problem is still persisting. 

The camera operation matrix is not so huge (80 sites for 310 days with a lot of zeros). 

I would appreciate any suggestions on how to build detection histories for several species (43) without the need to run the detection history function for each species. 

Cheers, 
Stef

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated.
parts:
Hi, 
This error is triggered when a record falls in an occasion that exceeds the number of columns in the effort/ detection matrix. So for example a record is calculated to be in occasion 11, but there are only 10 days available.
I don't know why that happens in your case, but can offer to have a look if you share a reproducible example. 

Does it also happen with longer occasions? I wouldn't be surprised if 2 days or longer work. And in general 1 day occasions rarely have any benefit at all, but have drawbacks such as very low parameter values for detection probability which may be hard to estimate and can cause model fitting to fail.

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated.
parts:
Hi Jurgen, 

thank you very much for your quick response. My feeling is that the error is not coming out as you suggested because:

1) I have created the camera operation matrix directly from the recordtable dataset, so a mismatch is impossible.

2) I have tried to increase the number of occasions up to ten, but it does not work either.

I have searched within the group for a similar question and the other users suggested that "holes" within the camera matrix operation causes the issues. 
In addition, when I have contacted you some months ago, I was able to ascertain that this issue arises when there are more than 10 problems within the camera matrix operation. 

I can try to build a reproducible example, but this will take some time.

Stef
 PS: in my case, collapsing more days is not possible cause the obs-covs varies between days.

Hi,
Things to check:
Does it happen with all species, or only one?
If only one, is there something unusual about the first/last record?
Does time zone UTC lead to the same error?
Does the argument day1 affect the outcome?
Does format of datetime column Match the default ymd HMS?

The issue with more than 10 problem columns was fixed here: :https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/commit/550d4aea2a614073c8b12454c7de3689bea56805


If you don't mind please share your R workspace privately via email so I can use the same data as you. You can remove all species but one that causes the error. Please also share the Code You used for camera operation.

Thank you,
Jürgen
